publications.title: Even flow in dynamic networks for wastewater treatment
publications.abstract:
Abstract
                  Network flow allocation is a central problem within operations research. Arguably, the most classic setting of flow allocation problems is a static one in which the arcs of a directed graph need to be assigned flow values in a way that respects the capacities of each edge and, for example, maximizes the amount of flow that arrives at a sink node. The numerous applications of flow problems have resulted in several variants being proposed and studied. In this paper, we study a variant of dynamic network flow. Dynamic network flow generalizes the static setting by introducing a notion of time and allowing the flow to move over time in the network. In our setting, the sink of the network also has a maximum capacity of flow it can receive at each timestep, and we are interested in computing flow allocations that distribute an even amount of flow to the sink of the network over all timesteps. Additionally, we assume that new flow can be generated at each non-sink node in each timestep, and that the nodes can temporarily store a limited amount of the flow. In a central instantiation of the problem, the non-sink nodes of the network are pumping stations that need to transfer wastewater to a treatment plant, which is the sink of the network. To evaluate our solving approaches in practice, we worked with the Helsinki Region Environmental Services Authority to collect and create a new open-source benchmark set based on wastewater quantities in the Helsinki region. More precisely, we study the applicability of linear programming for solving real-world benchmarks of this dynamic network flow optimization problem. As our main contributions, we: (i) extend and modify a previously proposed constraint model for computing feasible allocations to the dynamic setting and allow more flexible allocations, (ii) introduce several different approaches to even the workload arriving at the sink at each timestep, (iii) collect a new open-source dataset based on real-world wastewater flow quantities, and (iv) report on an extensive experimental evaluation of our model on three differently-sized time spans of the new dataset using state-of-the-art solvers. Our evaluation demonstrates that, among our evenness approaches, minimizing the difference between the maximum and minimum hourly incoming water to the treatment plant consistently yields the highest evenness in the flow arriving at the treatment plant. Additionally, we demonstrate the flexibility of our model by incorporating additional constraints aimed at reducing the energy consumption of the pumps.

publications.title: The Agent Internet A New Evolutionary Phase of the Web and Its Global Impact
publications.abstract: Large language model (LLM) based software agents are transitioning from one shot assistants to long term actors that plan, negotiate and accomplish tasks with multiple services. This transformation is resulting in what researchers call the Agent Internet, the Agentic Web or the Internet of Agents, in which programs are full-fledged players alongside people. This article summarizes academic surveys, industry studies and public market data from 2025 to 2026 to outline the multi-layered nature of this setup and to consider its pros and cons. According to market estimates, the revenue for agent software is estimated to be around eight billion dollars in 2025 and up to 35-53 billion dollars in 2030. Adoption statistics tell a tale of much experimentation and few pilots taking it to scale. We discuss communication protocols that enable agents to find and trust each other, the as yet undeveloped identity and payment layers and the burden of agent traffic on advertising supported content. But the challenges that we see are not just capabilities, but security, accountability, interoperability, and who pays for content and compute. Finally, we highlight some of the current research and policy gaps and suggest avenues for a responsible construction.

publications.title: Scientific Editor — AI Protocol (Agent Skill)
publications.abstract: An Agent Skill for editing and pre-submission auditing of scientific manuscripts in Russian and English. It verifies claims against sources and sources against reality, runs four gates (sources, internal facts, provenance and conflicts of interest, falsifiability), scores the text on a venue-calibrated rubric and returns an editorial recommendation. Bundled standard-library tools: a GOST-aware formatting linter and a version diff for reviewing edits.

publications.title: Evidence-Aware LLM Auditing of Commercial Promotion in Health Videos: De-identified Data and Reproducibility Materials
publications.abstract: De-identified data and offline reproducibility materials for Evidence-Aware LLM Auditing of Commercial Promotion in Health Videos: An Empirical Study. This single-platform study concerns a Chinese open social media platform and publication windows of September 10–23 in 2025 and 2026 (Beijing time). Contents: 260 evaluation records (20 calibration; 240 formal), 520 independent coder records, 67 nonblind error-review cells, and 633 linked-video records. The two video samples overlap and must not be added as independent cases. Only 96/633 linked records received frame screening. The package includes the joined analytic table, human coding manual v1.2, Chinese prompt templates with English translations, portable Python scripts, ten reference result tables, data dictionary, checksums and verification report. Fresh offline recomputation matches the ten reference tables and the joined analytic table. Raw video identifiers, creator names, URLs, source text, transcripts, quotations, precise timestamps, private linkage key, sampling seed and raw screening scores are withheld. This permits numerical recomputation, not sampling reconstruction, hosted-model reruns, classifier retraining or independent source interpretation. Historical gold_* fields are resolved reference labels, not error-free truth. Disease-claim fields are retained for transparency and excluded from primary analyses because independent kappa was zero. The 421 evaluation quotations and separate 490-quotation repair cohort are distinct. Repair outcomes are historical aggregates, not released quotation-level observations. Selective-review accuracy is retrospective agreement with an imperfect reference. See README.md for limitations and code/verify.py for reproduction checks. Version 1.0.0; CC BY 4.0. No external funding declared.
